+# BBuf Review Patterns (sgl-project/sglang, 2026-07-27 to 2026-10-30)
+
+Source: `bbuf-recent-review-corpus.jsonl.gz` (schema_version 2), a supplement to
+`references/sglang-review-corpus.jsonl.gz` (which stops at 2026-07-27T15:49Z).
+It holds 526 kept BBuf comments on 204 public PRs by other authors: 285 inline,
+125 review-submission bodies and 116 PR-conversation comments. Review states on
+those bodies: 63 APPROVED, 51 COMMENTED, 11 CHANGES_REQUESTED.
+
+Counts below come from keyword heuristics run over the kept comments and were
+spot-checked by hand. A comment can fall into more than one cluster, so treat
+the numbers as approximate. Percentages are out of 526 comments.
+
+## Recurring concerns
+
+| # | Concern | ~Comments | ~PRs |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| 1 | State lifecycle, stale caches, memory retention | 73 (14%) | 46 |
+| 2 | Tests that don't exercise the changed path | 66 (13%) | 56 |
+| 3 | Simplify, reuse existing helpers, remove dead or duplicate code | 67 (13%) | 41 |
+| 4 | Input contracts and fail-fast validation | 63 (12%) | 46 |
+| 5 | Silent behavior change or compatibility break | 55 (10%) | 39 |
+| 6 | Redundant or bloated tests; delete tests for trivial fixes | 53 (10%) | 41 |
+| 7 | Scope: split unrelated or independent changes | 52 (10%) | 37 |
+| 8 | CI coverage: registered, scheduled, actually executed | 51 (10%) | 41 |
+| 9 | Accuracy or parity evidence on real data | 45 (9%) | 41 |
+| 10 | PR description, naming, comments and docstrings | 38 (7%) | 32 |
+| 11 | Benchmark validity | 37 (7%) | 30 |
+| 12 | Housekeeping: lint, conflicts, rebase | 34 (6%) | 31 |
+| 13 | Platform and arch gating (SM, HIP/ROCm, OOT) | 28 (5%) | 24 |
+| 14 | Code placement (kernels/JIT tree, test directories) | 16 (3%) | 14 |
+| 15 | No new flags or env vars; auto-enable instead | 10 (2%) | 9 |
+
+### 1. State lifecycle and memory retention
+He asks for per-request or per-sample resets and for caches keyed on the real
+identity (effective config, file fingerprint). Memory must actually be released
+on offload or weight update. When a path can't be made coherent, he wants online
+weight updates rejected while it is enabled.
+- "`prev` is never cleared between samples, so each prompt's step 0 is compared with the previous prompt's final step, corrupting the fit." ([#36767](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36767#discussion_r3893894860))
+- "This reference keeps the packed CUDA storage alive after offload." ([#41339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41339#discussion_r4111515749))
+
+### 2. Tests that don't exercise the changed path
+His most PR-diverse concern: does the new test reach the modified branch? Common
+misses are mocks hiding the real kernel, eager-only tests for a graph-replay bug,
+parameters that skip the new path, and assertions too weak to fail. He usually
+names the case that would reach it.
+- "This test mocks the actual BSA call, so it doesn't validate the new per-query block counts." ([#35850](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35850#discussion_r3843054087))
+- "The current assertion only checks the NaN mask, so incorrect scales or zeroed finite outputs would still pass." ([#42689](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42689#discussion_r4213981663))
+
+### 3. Simplify, reuse, remove dead code
+He pushes back on abstractions with a single implementation, re-implemented
+utilities, duplicated or unreachable blocks, helpers nothing calls, long
+dispatch conditions, and hardcoded values.
+- "Do we need the abstract base class here when HostExpertStore is the only implementation?" ([#42557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42557#discussion_r4185116881))
+- "The second copy is unreachable after the first one sets `text_encoder`; please remove it." ([#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569#discussion_r3746345301)); see also "Nothing on this branch calls any of it" ([#39664](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39664#issuecomment-5699199068)).
+
+### 4. Input contracts and fail-fast validation
+This shows up mostly on kernel wrappers. He wants dtype, device, contiguity,
+alignment, stride and range checks, int32 overflow fixed, and nullptr
+arithmetic avoided. Unsupported input should be rejected explicitly instead of
+crashing or producing garbage. `can_use_*` predicates should return False and
+never raise.
+- "A bad caller can get silent garbage or an illegal access instead of a fail-fast error." ([#32327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32327#discussion_r3746324925))
+- "`can_use_*` should return `False`, not raise." ([#38182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38182#discussion_r3947940175))
+
+### 5. Silent behavior change or compatibility break
+He flags paths that silently ignore input, fall back, override a documented
+contract, or break existing callers (Python/CLI, other models, OOT platforms).
+A warning is not enough for him: he wants the combination rejected or the old
+behavior preserved.
+- "a warning alone still returns approximate output under the lossless label." ([#36767](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36767#discussion_r3904549241))
+- "We silently ignore every reference image after the first." ([#33386](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33386#discussion_r3802683813))
+
+### 6. Redundant or bloated tests
+Either a terse delete request (the fix is small and safe, or the test is a
+one-off script), or a cleanup ask: consolidate into existing files and fixtures,
+parameterize, cut long docstrings, aim for 2–3 files (CPU/kernel/e2e). These
+comments grew from about mid-September, as large generated test files became
+common.
+- "The pr's change is small and safe, we don't need to add this test. Can you delete it?" ([#43640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43640#discussion_r4259783756))
+- "It's 253 lines for four cases, with quite a bit of repeated setup and explanation." ([#39889](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39889#issuecomment-5842692218)); "The goal is the smallest test set that catches the actual failures" ([#44887](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44887#issuecomment-6310538178)).
+
+### 7. Scope: split unrelated changes
+He asks for unrelated tweaks to be dropped, independent optimizations and opt-in
+paths to go to follow-up PRs, overlap with already-merged PRs to be removed, and
+the change made less invasive. He does not want one PR per bug, though: related
+fixes stay together, each with its regression test.
+- "Could we drop this unrelated tolerance change from this PR?" ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994#discussion_r3695669279))
+- "Please split along those boundaries, keeping each regression with its fix; one PR per individual bug is unnecessary." ([#44309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44309#pullrequestreview-5596043291))
+
+### 8. CI coverage: registered and actually executed
+`test/manual` files don't run in CI. Registered tests need the `__main__` entry
+point, the right `runner_config` (for example an SM120 runner for SM120 code),
+and the right `test/registered/...` directory. He also wants evidence that the
+new GPU cases ran on the current head rather than being skipped. Many approvals
+end with "please wait for the relevant (AMD/GPU) CI".
+- "Could we move a focused fusion test to `test/registered`? `test/manual` is not covered by CI." ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994#discussion_r3695667716))
+- "Therefore the file can run in CI, but the newly added SM120 admission is not actually exercised." ([#34327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34327#issuecomment-5264760664))
+
+### 9. Accuracy and parity evidence
+For numerics, default-on flags or kernel swaps, he asks for real-dataset accuracy
+(GSM8K, AIME, MMLU) with the flag on vs off. He also wants the results rerun on
+the current head instead of an earlier revision, plus output or logprob parity.
+- "Can you add some real datasets such as AIME or GMS8K's accuracy comparison results?" ([#33436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33436#issuecomment-5199438786))
+- "Since this is now default-on and changes the accumulation order, can we add a model-level accuracy comparison with the flag on and off?" ([#34331](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34331#discussion_r3764661208))
+
+### 10. Description, naming, comments, docstrings
+He wants the PR description to match the code (Risk section, scope claims), and
+asks about unexplained renames. Names should carry scope (a `dllm_` prefix, or
+the kernel's real purpose). Comments and docstrings should be short or removed,
+and docs should point to the existing page.

+Both arms must use the same graph mode, the baseline must be the real pre-PR

+### 12. Housekeeping
+These are one-liners: "Please fix lint", "Please fix conflict", "Could you rebase

+### 13. Platform and arch gating

+Kernels belong in the `sglang/kernels` tree, with JIT preferred over AOT

+`test/registered/unit/layers/...`.
+- "Can you remove this kernel to jit?" ([#38040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38040#discussion_r4145875547)); "Can we move it to sglang/kernel?" ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219#discussion_r3662245831))

+If an optimization is safe, he wants it enabled automatically when applicable.

+- "Can we avoid add this environ?" ([#42929](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42929#discussion_r4361082342))
+
+## Tone and format habits
+
+- **Questions over commands.** About 43% of comments contain a "Could we / Can we
+  / Should we …?" question, and 22% open with one. "Please …" shows up in 33%,
+  mostly in summaries and follow-ups.
+- **Brevity by default.** The median length is 266 chars inline, 224 for review
+  bodies and 494 for conversation. 66 comments are 80 chars or less and 190 are
+  200 or less. Test cleanup and housekeeping get one-liners such as "Can we delete
+  this test?", "Please fix lint" and "Please clean up the test". The English in
+  these is informal and unpolished ("Can we avoid add this environ?").
+- **Evidence-first findings.** He states the concrete failure (shape, value,
+  config, rank count) before the ask, e.g. "This should break TP=7: the layer
+  expects 480 features and receives 3360." ([#33182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33182#discussion_r3802683190)).
+  He often reproduces it himself (25 comments): "I tried `topk=64` on H200: this
+  check accepts it, then the `KU_ASSERT` calls `exit(1)` and kills the process."
+  ([#32327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32327#discussion_r3746324923)).
+- **States what he did not validate.** 36 comments do this, e.g. "I haven't run
+  the GPU tests." ([#42557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42557#pullrequestreview-5416093875)),
+  "CPU function checks only; no LingBot/GPU run." ([#44888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44888#pullrequestreview-5596042787))
+- **Severity tags.** `[P1]`/`[P2]` appear in 36 comments, all from mid-September
+  onward. `Non-blocking:` appears in 27 (mostly October), and `nit:`/`nits:` is
+  rare. Even blocking comments are usually phrased as requests rather than
+  demands.
+- **Review summary bodies are pointers.** COMMENTED and CHANGES_REQUESTED bodies
+  are often one line that frames the inline comments: "A few cache edge cases."
+  ([#34274](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34274#pullrequestreview-4924860684)),
+  "Two input-contract edge cases below." In September about 7 long reviews used
+  a "Change summary + Mermaid flowchart" layout.
+- **Approvals carry a reason plus a residual ask.** Of 63 approvals with a body,
+  29 start with "LGTM", usually followed by one sentence on why the fix is
+  correct. 33 mention CI ("Let's wait for CI", "Please run the AMD CI before
+  merging"), and he often adds a follow-up to keep ("Please keep that regression
+  test"). He rarely requests changes: 11 of 125 bodies.
+- **Hands-on maintainer actions.** About 68 comments report his own work:
+  "Targeted validation for `<sha>`" with `/rerun-test`, independent GPU
+  validation reports, pushed rebases or fixes, and fix PRs on the
+  contributor's fork.
+- **Language.** All comments in this window are in English.
+
+## Implications for `sglang-humanize-review`
+
+1. Check that each new or changed test reaches the modified branch: no mock in
+   place of the real code, graph replay where the bug lives, inputs that hit the
+   new path, and assertions that can fail.
+2. Flag redundant or bloated tests. Suggest deleting tests for small, safe
+   fixes, and otherwise consolidating them into existing files and fixtures.
+3. Check CI wiring: `test/registered` placement, a `__main__` entry, a runner
+   for the target arch, and proof the test ran on the current head.
+4. Prefer auto-enabling over new flags or env vars, and require accuracy
+   evidence for anything default-on.
+5. Ask for unrelated changes to be split out, but keep related fixes together.
+6. Audit benchmarks: same graph mode in both arms, a real pre-PR baseline,
+   production shapes, commands and SHAs.
+7. Use his register: a short question that states the concrete failure, a
+   `[P1]`/`[P2]`/`Non-blocking` tag when it matters, a one-line review body,
+   and a note on what was not validated.

+# Maintainer Standards for SGLang Reviews (required reading)
+
+These are the current review standards of SGLang maintainer BBuf, distilled
+from three sources, all as of 2026-10-30:
+
+- his refactor and cleanup PRs ([refactor-conventions.md](refactor-conventions.md)),
+- the 526 review comments he left on 204 other authors' PRs after the main corpus
+  cutoff ([bbuf-review-patterns.md](bbuf-review-patterns.md), raw episodes in
+  `bbuf-recent-review-corpus.jsonl.gz`),
+- the review requirements he gave his coding agents.
+
+**Precedence.** When these standards and an older corpus precedent disagree,
+follow these standards: they describe how the codebase and the review bar look
+now. The corpus still decides subsystem-specific risk; these rules decide
+structure, tests, evidence and tone.
+
+## 1. Review order
+
+1. Understand the PR: what it does, which code it changes, the risks, and which
+   key validation is missing. On a re-review, map each earlier comment to the
+   fix and its location, and judge whether the fix is reasonable.
+2. For AI-generated PRs (most incoming PRs), check structure and tests before
+   logic: does the code sit where the current layout says, and do the tests
+   prove anything? Then correctness.
+3. Check reachability first: if nothing calls the new path, it is dead code.
+4. Give an explicit verdict on merge risk.
+
+## 2. Scope and size
+
+- Every touched file outside the feature (CI scripts, unrelated tests, unrelated
+  tolerances) needs a stated reason; otherwise ask to revert it to main.
+- Keep intrusion into the main runtime small and changes general. Question a
+  backend, flag or optimization added for a single model.
+- Push for the smallest diff and the fewest files. Ask to drop non-general
+  optimizations that show no clear gain.
+- Split unrelated or independent changes into follow-ups, but keep related
+  fixes together, each with its regression test. Tiny near-duplicate PRs can be
+  folded into one ([#44309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44309#pullrequestreview-5596043291)).
+- Ask for verbose, over-defensive code to be heavily simplified: single-
+  implementation abstract base classes, re-implemented utilities, duplicated or
+  unreachable blocks, helpers nothing calls, long dispatch conditions.
+
+## 3. Placement and structure (details in refactor-conventions.md)
+
+Check every new file and import against the current layout:
+
+- Kernels live under `python/sglang/kernels`, are imported from
+  `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>`, and are grouped by complete computation, never by
+  model (no `ops/<model>/` directory). `sglang.jit_kernel`, `srt/**/triton_ops`
+  and kernels defined under `srt/` or `multimodal_gen/` are retired. Prefer JIT
+  over new AOT `sgl-kernel` code.
+- Kernel integration code, including wrappers for external libraries, belongs in
+  the kernels tree, not `srt/`. Kernels never import `sglang.srt`; runtime state
+  is passed in as arguments.
+- New public kernel entry points register a lazy `KernelSpec`; a new group
+  updates `ops._GROUPS` and the kernels README in the same PR.
+- Multi-backend operators subclass `BaseFusedOp` with a real `forward_native`;
+  backend methods (`forward_<backend>`) and platform methods (`forward_cuda`,
+  `forward_hip`, ...) stay separate.
+- Input contracts (dtype, device, contiguity, shape, stride, alignment, int32
+  range) are enforced in the kernel's host launcher and fail fast. `can_use_*`
+  gates only answer "is this kernel applicable", return `False` rather than
+  raise, and never restate operand contracts or swallow errors into a silent
+  fallback.
+- Diffusion code imports kernels only from the `ops.diffusion` facade; every
+  non-bit-exact fusion goes through `sites/` with a declared quality tier.
+- MoE gate/top-k goes through the single Triton router; retired per-model gate
+  kernels must not come back.
+- Moves use `git mv` plus import rewrites with no forwarding shim, and update
+  every reference (patch strings, spec targets, tuning paths, CODEOWNERS, CI
+  filters) in the same PR.
+
+## 4. Flags, env vars and dispatch
+
+- Do not add new environment variables, `SGLANG_DISABLE_*` kill switches or
+  `server_args`. Enable a safe optimization automatically from GPU arch, shape
+  and backend conditions, and limit dispatch to the measured winning range
+  ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994#discussion_r3695671794)).
+- If an env var is truly needed, it is declared in `srt/environ.py` or
+  `multimodal_gen/envs.py` with the `SGLANG_` prefix and read through `envs`.
+- A path that changes numerics stays opt-in until model-level accuracy evidence
+  exists; default-on changes need accuracy with the flag on and off.
+- Use exact capability checks, not range arithmetic (`sm_version // 10 == 12`
+  is too broad); never read a HIP/MUSA major as a CUDA SM version; keep
+  ROCm/XPU/OOT dispatch intact. An auto backend must not pick a configuration
+  that startup later rejects.
+- If invasive code is unavoidable, name it by its scope (for example `dllm_*`).
+
+## 5. Tests
+
+- Admit a test only if you can name the production change that would turn it
+  red. Ask to delete: mock-only call-choreography tests, interface or
+  attribute-existence tests, input-legality tests, tautologies and source-shape
+  tests. Expect AI-generated test code to shrink by roughly 90%.
+- Check that each new test reaches the modified branch: no mock in front of the
+  real kernel or executor, CUDA-graph replay when the bug lives there,
+  parameters that hit the new path, and assertions on values rather than masks
+  or shapes ([#42689](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42689#discussion_r4213981663),
+  [#35850](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35850#discussion_r3843054087)).
+- For a small, safe fix, or a narrow kernel unlikely to change, ask to delete the
+  new per-PR CI test ([#43640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43640#discussion_r4259783756)).
+  Do keep the regression test that reproduces a fixed bug, and keep meaningful
+  existing assertions.
+- Prefer extending existing test files and fixtures (parametrize, `subTest`)
+  over new files; aim for a few files (CPU / kernel / e2e). Ask to shorten long
+  generated test files ([#39889](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39889#issuecomment-5842692218)).
+- Tests live in the registered layout (`test/registered/kernels/ops/<group>/`,
+  `test/registered/unit/<subsystem>/`, `e2e/...`); `test/manual` does not run in
+  CI. Registered files need a literal `register_*_ci(...)` call, a `__main__`
+  that runs the tests, and a runner whose hardware matches the code's gates.
+  Merged test files inherit the union of their sources' CI lanes.
+
+## 6. Evidence in the PR description
+
+- The description must match the current head (scope, default-on/off, Risk
+  section) and include the exact launch and benchmark commands with base and
+  head SHAs.
+- Performance claims: measured on the hardware the PR targets, across several
+  models and concurrency levels, against the strongest tuned baseline and SGLang
+  main (not other frameworks), both arms in the same graph mode, production
+  shapes, cold L2 on an uncontended GPU, and no credit for optimizations that
+  already landed ([#37903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37903#discussion_r3963789174),
+  [#35760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35760#discussion_r3826477180)).
+- Keep only changes that improve both the kernel and end-to-end numbers; a
+  kernel that regresses anywhere stays at main. Kernel PRs show microbenchmark
+  and correctness results; a PR with no speedup should be closed.
+- Numerics changes show real-dataset accuracy (GSM8K, AIME, MMLU) and, for
+  replacement kernels, bitwise equality where feasible and unchanged speculative
+  accept length. Rerun after a rebase; results from an earlier revision do not
+  count.
+- Diffusion PRs show kernel and end-to-end numbers plus rendered image or video
+  comparisons against main.
+- Refactor and cleanup PRs prove equivalence (byte/AST-identical moves, output
+  hashes, the same failing tests as main) and list the platforms not validated.
+
+## 7. CI coverage and the merge bar
+
+- A PR is mergeable when the tests related to the change actually passed on the
+  current head, every other failure is shown to be unrelated to the diff, there
+  is no conflict, and it has an approval. Optional unrelated jobs do not need to
+  be green.
+- Skipped, cancelled, zero-test and `run-ci` gate-failed jobs are not passes.
+  Ask for proof that new GPU cases executed on this head, linked to the job.
+- Related tests are triggered together, only the files the change touches.
+- When validation has started, the head is pinned; updating main is for an
+  approved PR whose CI breaks on a stale base.
+
+## 8. Writing review comments
+
+- English, inline at the exact code location, short and plain: the concrete
+  failure (shape, value, config, rank count), then the ask, usually as a
+  question ("Could we ...?", "Can we delete this test?"). No AI flavor, no
+  headings or filler.
+- Severity tags: `[P1]` must fix, `[P2]` should fix, `Non-blocking:` for advice,
+  `Nit:` rarely. Raise only what must change; the goal is approve plus CI.
+- A review body is one line that points at the inline comments ("A few cache
+  edge cases.").
+- An approval says why it is correct in one sentence, adds a one-line TODO when
+  something should follow, and names the CI still to wait for ("LGTM. ... Let's
+  wait for the AMD CI.").
+- Say what you did not validate ("CPU-only checks; no GPU run.").
+- Housekeeping is a one-liner: "Please fix lint", "Please fix conflict", "Could
+  you rebase this PR onto the latest main branch?".

+# SGLang layout and cleanup conventions from BBuf's refactor PRs (2026-06 to 2026-10)
+
+Rules from merged refactor and cleanup PRs in `sgl-project/sglang`, plus the guard tests and lints they added, for reviewers to apply to incoming diffs. Source of truth on `main`:
+
+- `python/sglang/kernels/README.md`
+- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/README.md`
+- `test/README.md`
+- the `kernel-organization` skill
+
+Each rule gives **Why**, **Detect** (what to look for in the diff) and **Src** (public PRs).
+
+## 1. Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`)
+
+**KR1. Import callable kernels from `sglang.kernels.ops.<group>`, and add new kernels there.**
+- Why: RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630) made `sglang.kernels` the single home for kernels. All `srt/**/triton_ops` trees and about 280 scattered kernels were moved in, and `sglang.jit_kernel` was deleted.
+- Detect:
+  - `from sglang.jit_kernel`, or a new `triton_ops/` directory.
+  - A new `@triton.jit`, CuTe-DSL or `load_jit(...)` kernel defined under `srt/` or `multimodal_gen/`.
+  - Runtime code calling `sgl_kernel` directly where an `ops.<group>` wrapper exists.
+  - Exceptions: the `sgl_kernel` wheel API and vendored trees.
+- Src: [#30044](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30044), [#30784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30784)–[#30795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30795), [#31582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31582), [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#26000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26000).
+
+**KR2. Group an operator by its complete computation, not by the model that first used it.** The rules:
+- Any cross-rank collective or peer-memory access goes in `communication`.
+- A producer plus its output quantization stays with the producer: norm+quant in `layernorm`, act+quant in `activation`, a quant-epilogue GEMM in `gemm`, MoE dispatch+quant in `moe`.
+- `quantization` holds only pure format conversion.
+- RoPE and QK-norm+RoPE go in `attention`.
+- `kvcache` owns ops that read or write cache contents. `attention` owns page tables, `cu_seqlens` and `kv_indices`.
+- A GEMM or GEMV and its tuning JSON go in `gemm`.
+
+Further notes:
+- Why: model-named bundles and misfiled ops kept drifting back in.
+- Detect:
+  - A new `kernels/ops/<model>/` directory, or a `.py` placed directly in `ops/`.
+  - A quantized GEMM under `quantization/`, or an all-reduce-fused kernel outside `communication/`.
+  - Do not flag a model-named *file* inside the right group.
+- Src: [#45112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45112), [#41243](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41243), [#32148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32148).
+
+**KR3. A new group or top-level `kernels/` directory updates `ops._GROUPS`, the README group list and the README Layout block in the same PR.**
+- Why: `test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py` fails otherwise:
+  - `test_readme_operator_groups_match_registry`
+  - `test_readme_layout_lists_every_top_level_directory`
+  - `test_operator_and_test_groups_agree`: no `.py` directly in `ops/`, and every test or benchmark subdirectory must be a real group.
+- Detect: a new directory with no README or `_GROUPS` change.
+- Src: [#45112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45112), [#32788](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32788).
+
+**KR4. Register every public entry point with a lazy `KernelSpec(op="<group>.<name>", backend=..., target="module:attr")`, and keep group imports metadata-only.**
+
+Why: guard tests enforce this, and the registry is checked too:
+- `test_import_stays_metadata_only` fails if importing `sglang.kernels.ops` loads `sgl_kernel`, `sglang.kernels.jit`, cutlass, flydsl or aiter.
+- `test_inventory_targets_survive_module_moves` fails on stale targets.
+- `test_reclassified_public_entry_points_are_inventoried` requires specs for public functions. Names starting with `_`, `can_`, `is_` or `use_` are exempt.
+- The registry rejects conflicting registrations for the same op and backend.
+
+Detect:
+- A new public function in `kernels/ops/**` with no spec, or heavy imports in a group `__init__.py`.
+- Write-only metadata (`description=`, `FormatSignature`), which #44690 deleted.
+- Inline CUDA-only frozensets instead of `spec.CUDA_ONLY`.
+

+## 2. Fused ops (`BaseFusedOp`)
+
+**F1. A multi-backend operator subclasses `sglang.kernels.fused_op.BaseFusedOp` and implements a real pure-torch `forward_native`.**

+**F2. Keep kernel backends and platform paths separate.**
+- Kernel backends are `forward_<backend>` methods (`forward_triton`, `forward_jit`, `forward_torch_npu`, …).
+- Platform paths are `forward_cuda`, `forward_hip`, `forward_npu`, `forward_xpu`, `forward_musa` and `forward_cpu`.

+
+**D1. Import diffusion kernels only from the `sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion` facade, never from a submodule.**

+**D2. Lay out `ops/diffusion` by operator domain, with the backend as a filename suffix.**

+**G1. Declare env vars in `srt/environ.py` or `multimodal_gen/envs.py` with the `SGLANG_` prefix and a typed `Env*`, and read them through `envs`.**

+**G2. Delete dead code completely, and give zero-consumer internals no shim.**
+- "Completely" means the code, its flag, docs rows, tests, CI filters and registry entries.
+- First check callers, including string targets and dynamic lookups.
+- Only user-facing CLI or config surfaces get a deprecated alias.
